extracted.intended_audience: USPTO leadership, patent practitioners, policymakers, and other stakeholders interested in patent system performance and reform
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria used by the Patent Public Advisory Committee (PPAC) to assess U.S. patent system performance, including patent quality, pendency, PTAB operations, IT/AI, outreach, innovation expansion, legislative and finance matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality patent (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A quality patent is one that was thoroughly examined and prosecuted at the application for patent stage that can withstand post-issuance challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality patents afford patent holders reasonable reliance that they hold enforceable rights and inform the public of the metes and bounds of duly issued patents to avoid infringement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent quality measurement — compliance with statutory requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent quality reflects the extent to which the USPTO, at the application and prosecution stage, correctly rejects applications that fail to meet statutory requirements and issues patents for those applications that do meet statutory requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO has goals for compliance of work product; each year the USPTO reviews a random sample of work product to evaluate compliance. Performance on these metrics (e.g., OPQA reviews, internal sampling) is a core measure of quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Durability of issued patents (post-issuance quality)
rubrics_metrics.description: A true assessment of patent quality must consider whether issued patents are durable — i.e., able to withstand post-issuance invalidity and patentability challenges (for PPAC this assessment is limited to internal challenges such as PTAB proceedings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare front-end examination outcomes to back-end PTAB decisions to identify inconsistencies; durability is measured by whether issued patents survive post-issuance review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pendency metrics and goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Pendency refers to the amount of time an application is pending before the USPTO. The USPTO maintains short-term average pendency goals and long-term absolute pendency goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance is tracked via metrics such as monthly pendency of applications, application volume, and petition processing; reducing pendency across all applications is an objective, supplemented by absolute long-term targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bridging/closing the gap between Patents and PTAB
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and remove inconsistencies between the Patents business unit and the PTAB by improving continuity across units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actions include data collection and data sharing between units, making IT systems and data formats compatible, establishing a two-way learning loop, cross-training staff, co-implementing initiatives and pilots, and engaging external stakeholders for feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection, data sharing, and compatible IT systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective quality assessment and collaboration require compatible IT systems and data formats between Patents and PTAB so that data can be collected and shared readily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upgrading PTAB IT to be compatible with Patents' system and moving toward common formats supports two-way learning and reduces inconsistencies; this supports AI initiatives and overall efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-training between Patents and PTAB
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-training staff between the Patent Examining Corps and Administrative Patent Judges to foster understanding and consistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-training is part of closing the gap, enabling a shared understanding of statutory application and reducing divergent outcomes between front-end examination and back-end review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant role in quality — education and outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants, inventors, and their representatives play a role in patent quality through improved submissions and prosecution practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO-provided programs such as Stakeholder Training on Examination Practice and Procedure (STEPP) and virtual instructor-led training (vILT) are encouraged; stakeholders should provide feedback about these programs' usefulness and additional needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB consistency with Patents — uniform application of statutory requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The PTAB should apply statutory requirements consistently with Patents to avoid an internal 'gap' between examination and post-issuance decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPAC evaluates perceived inconsistencies and recommends initiatives (data sharing, training, policy alignment) to ensure consistent application of law and practice across the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB Director review and remedy after Arthrex
rubrics_metrics.description: Following United States v. Arthrex, Inc., the Director has discretion to review decisions rendered by Administrative Patent Judges and issue final decisions on behalf of the PTAB to address appointment-structure concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PPAC emphasizes the importance of a Director capable of making critical policy and administrative decisions and notes the operational disruption caused by absence of a fully appointed Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arthrex holding (Appointments Clause remedy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Arthrex held APJs are 'inferior officers' but that lack of Director oversight rendered their appointment unconstitutional; remedy: Director can review and issue final decisions for PTAB matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This decision affects PTAB governance and underscores the need for clear processes for Director review to cure constitutional defects while preserving functioning review procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAS Institute (IPR institution scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the USPTO institutes an IPR, it must decide the patentability of all the claims the petitioner challenged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO and PTAB practice must reflect SAS: institute decisions should address every challenged claim, which impacts institution decisions and case management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cuozzo (BRI standard and appealability of institution)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Supreme Court upheld the USPTO regulation requiring the PTAB to apply the broadest reasonable interpretation (BRI) standard in IPR proceedings and held that the decision to institute an IPR is not appealable to federal courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes interpretation standards for claim construction in AIA proceedings and limits interlocutory judicial review of institution decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thryv (timeliness of AIA petitions is unreviewable)
rubrics_metrics.description: SCOTUS held the USPTO has unreviewable authority to decide whether a party properly petitioned under the AIA within one year of being served an infringement complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instituting or denying petitions on timeliness grounds is agency-final and generally not subject to judicial review, affecting strategic considerations in filing post-grant petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return Mail (government as petitioner excluded)
rubrics_metrics.description: SCOTUS held that a government agency cannot challenge patents using IPR, PGR, and CBM because statutory references to 'person' exclude the government or any agency thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limits who may bring post-grant challenges and informs policy and litigant strategy regarding government involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv factors (consideration when parallel district court pending)
rubrics_metrics.description: PTAB applies Fintiv factors when considering whether to deny institution of a petition under 35 U.S.C. § 314(a) when a district court proceeding is pending in parallel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sotera (precedential) addressed how to apply these factors; PPAC monitors PTAB's application of Fintiv to ensure appropriate case-management balancing between forums.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amgen v. Sanofi — enablement standard for functional claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Amgen held that patent claims that claim antibodies by what they bind to were invalid under 35 U.S.C. § 112 for lack of enablement because it would take undue experimentation to identify which of millions of candidates bind to a specific protein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sets a high bar for enablement of broad functional claiming (e.g., antibodies) and affects examination and post-issuance review standards on enablement and undue experimentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Yu v. Apple — §101 application to mechanical/digital inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Yu held that a patent directed to a tangible digital camera was invalid under 35 U.S.C. § 101 for covering the abstract idea of enhancing photographs, signaling that §101 challenges may be applied to mechanical patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision opens the door to more §101 challenges and informs patent eligibility analysis in examination and post-issuance proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mylan Labs v. Janssen — appealability of denial of institution
rubrics_metrics.description: Mylan held that PTAB decisions not to institute an IPR are not appealable to the Federal Circuit for lack of subject matter jurisdiction; mandamus remains possible but is 'especially difficult to satisfy.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This constrains appellate avenues for petitioners denied institution and impacts strategy for challenging institution denials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trimble — licensing demand letters and personal jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Trimble made it easier for alleged infringers to file declaratory judgment actions in desired venues by holding that a patentee’s repeated contact (multiple patent licensing demand letters) in an alleged infringer’s home venue can be sufficient to provide minimum contacts for personal jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent holders should be mindful of venue and jurisdictional implications of licensing outreach; this affects enforcement strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB quality improvement initiatives — continuous learning, rulemaking, programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality improvement initiatives at the PTAB include 'Enabling Continuous Learning,' rulemaking, and programs intended to improve decision quality and operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initiatives encompass internal and external training, program development, and procedural rule updates to promote consistent, high-quality adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB operational efforts and IT improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational efforts to improve PTAB include IT improvements/upgrades, hearings operations, PTAB website improvements, and external/internal training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IT upgrades (including compatibility with Patents systems), improved hearing processes, and better online resources are recommended to enhance transparency and efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte appeals oversight and metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Track statistics and ongoing activities for ex parte appeals to monitor performance and identify areas for outreach and improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPAC expects data-driven monitoring of ex parte appeals, outreach to stakeholders, and initiatives to reduce backlogs or inefficiencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Technology criteria — cybersecurity, resilience, cloud migration, DOCX
rubrics_metrics.description: IT priorities include strengthening cybersecurity, improving resilience, migrating to the cloud, and supporting modern document formats (DOCX).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sustainable funding and investment in IT are necessary to support agency operations, prevent cyber-attacks, and enable modernization (including compatibility for data sharing and AI tools).

rubrics_metrics.name: Artificial Intelligence criteria — auto-classification, AI-assisted search, policy development
rubrics_metrics.description: AI initiatives include auto-classification, AI for patent search, and the development of AI-related policies and regulations to address inventorship and examination needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Building and implementing robust AI systems requires sustainable funding, full staffing of AI technical and strategic experts, and cross-unit data sharing; PPAC recommends these to improve efficiencies and stakeholder access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developing AI policies at the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO must define, build, and implement AI policies to guide internal use of AI tools and address AI-related inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy development should consider data governance, transparency, stakeholder access, ethical considerations, and alignment with international practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation Expansion — diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) of inventorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Make USPTO services more accessible to those lacking resources, know-how, or sophistication; increase demonstrable progress in inventor diversity across demographics, geography, and economic conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPAC supports the Innovation Expansion Subcommittee and initiatives like the Expanding Innovation Hub, scholarships, virtual programming, and outreach to underrepresented innovators; collaboration with the Council for Inclusive Innovation (CI2) is encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional outreach and international engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Expand and support USPTO Regional Offices and international engagement (e.g., IP & Trade, IP5 and ID5, WIPO work-sharing) to facilitate stakeholder access and global cooperation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regional offices should provide local outreach; international work-sharing and participation in forums (IP5/ID5/WIPO) supports harmonization and operational cooperation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative monitoring and suggested statutory initiatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor and advise on pending legislation and congressional activities affecting patent policy (e.g., patent bar eligibility changes, subject matter eligibility studies, sequenced examination pilot program, patent small claims tribunal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPAC tracks hearings, pending bills, and statutory studies and recommends Congress make previously collected user fees available to USPTO; PPAC provides input to legislative bodies on policy proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finance — budget status, fee adjustments, reserves and access to collected fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess USPTO's budget status, historical trends, fee adjustments, and previously collected fees not available; target reserve levels (for Patents defined as three months of operating requirements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPAC recommends Congress provide access to previously collected user fees to reach optimal reserve levels, improve infrastructure, and mitigate economic uncertainty; fee policy should align with operational modernization needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of metrics and transparency — measuring performance by quality and pendency
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO's performance is commonly measured by the twin metrics of pendency and quality, and these should be transparently reported and analyzed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPAC uses metrics (monthly pendency, quality sampling results, volumes, petitions) to evaluate agency performance and recommend improvements; transparency helps stakeholders assess agency effectiveness.
